statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-2007 (PostgreSQL pg_trgm heap buffer overflow writes pattern onto server memory) affects only PostgreSQL 18.0 and 18.1: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-2007/ says PostgreSQL 18.1 and 18.0 are affected and lists a fix only for major version 18, and the PostgreSQL 17 release notes do not list it. The fix commits, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/00896ddaf41fa7b725991120678d544c18c6af70 and https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/54598670fe0a191f49848d1a1a8ab09d99616e71, say they are backpatched to version 18 and no further because in earlier versions pg_trgm lower-cased a string one character at a time, so the lower-cased string never had more characters than the input; that changed in version 18 with commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/fb1a18810f07fc3b722392103d67ce8ed188b63d, which is not in the REL_17_12 release tag. The Debian tracker records postgresql-17 as not affected, vulnerable code not present: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-2007. We checked every published postgresql17 build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0) on both x86_64 and aarch64, with package checksums verified against the package index: each server binary reports the PostgreSQL 17 release of the same version, and pg_trgm.so in the postgresql17-contrib package of every build references lowerstr_with_len, the PostgreSQL 17 routine that lower-cases each character in place (src/backend/tsearch/ts_locale.c at REL_17_12), and not str_tolower, the routine version 18 switched to, while its own show_trgm, our control, is present in every build. Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, lists this CVE under its 17.8-r0 and 17.9-r0 secfixes, but no code change for this CVE was applied to the PostgreSQL 17 branch: the only REL_17_STABLE commit whose Security trailer names it, https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/a3acb409025a2f8e2cb93346bbc1d87281f861fc, changes only the 17.8 release notes and does not mention this CVE, and the 17.8 and 17.9 release notes do not list it.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-2007 (PostgreSQL pg_trgm heap buffer overflow writes pattern onto server memory) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 18.2: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-2007/ lists 18.2 as the fixed release for major version 18, and the 18.2 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.2/, include it. Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-2007 under its 18.2-r0 secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD from the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version, and the postgres server binary in each published build (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports that PostgreSQL release. The pg_trgm module is present: pg_trgm.so ships in the postgresql18-contrib package of every published build for Alpine 3.23, on both x86_64 and aarch64. 18.2-r0, built from PostgreSQL 18.2, is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 carrying the fix. The earlier published build for Alpine 3.23 (18.1-r0) is built from an earlier PostgreSQL 18 release and is recorded as affected.
